key_insight: There is no universal best surrogate for transient flows under time-varying boundary conditions; the right architecture depends on whether the flow is boundary-driven or phase-memory dominated.
engineering_relevance: For CFD surrogates in manufacturing and vortex-shedding applications, model choice and validation should be matched to the flow physics, not just pointwise error.
method: Compared 8 surrogate architectures on two transient benchmark flows: 3D CMP slurry film and 2D Karman vortex street.
Varied two design axes: full-field vs latent-state learning, and one-shot vs autoregressive time prediction.
Evaluated models with five physics-oriented criteria: field, structure, invented motion, amplitude, and timing.
evidence_signal: A one-shot full-field model achieved 3.2% relative error on cumulative wall shear stress in CMP, while a latent autoregressive DeepONet preserved 96% of shedding power in KVS that other models nearly eliminated.
watch_item: Offline training cost is substantial, so practical payoff depends on how many post-training queries are needed and may not generalize beyond the tested regimes.
paper_title: No Free Lunch in Flow Surrogates under Time-Varying Boundary Conditions: A Two-Regime Study
